title: Difficult Airway: Oxygenation and Backup Planning
subject: Anesthesia
preview: A difficult airway plan prioritizes oxygenation, patient preparation, operator skill and backup strategies.
quickRevision: A difficult airway plan prioritizes oxygenation, patient preparation, operator skill and backup strategies.
Failed intubation pathways require clear limits on repeated attempts and timely rescue ventilation.
Team communication, equipment readiness and escalation pathways are as important as a single device choice.

sections.title: Clinical syndrome and red flags
points: A difficult airway plan prioritizes oxygenation, patient preparation, operator skill and backup strategies.
Assessment includes mouth opening, neck mobility, airway pathology, physiology and aspiration risk.

sections.title: Differentiate and manage
points: Failed intubation pathways require clear limits on repeated attempts and timely rescue ventilation.
Team communication, equipment readiness and escalation pathways are as important as a single device choice.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Successful tracheal tube placement is not the only goal; maintaining oxygenation is central.

quiz.question: What is the overriding priority in managing a difficult airway?
quiz.explanation: Maintain oxygenation. A difficult airway plan prioritizes oxygenation, patient preparation, operator skill and backup strategies.
